newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen opening under pressure.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen opening under pressure.

* Toronto stocks were seen opening lower as focus shifted back to stock performance after two days of Greenspan-driven gains. * Traders said banks and paper companies may show strength.
Toronto stocks were expected to open lower on Thursday as focus shifted back to the stocks themselves after two days of gains driven by U.S. Federal Reserve Chaiman Alan Greenspan.
Traders said reality should start to set in as investors digest what Greenspan said in his testimony to Congress.

"I think basically what he said is he doesn't see a whole lot of inflation this year, but if the market is six months forward-looking, that's 1998, and (in) 1998 we could see the economy slow. And if the economy slows, there could still be some inflation, even if it does moderate," one trader said.
Toronto stocks ventured into record territory on Wednesday amid Greenspan-driven expectations that Canadian and U.S. interest rates would not move higher soon.
The TSE 300 Composite Index added 50.91 points to finish at 6765.16, surpassing the previous record close on July 17.
The trader said Toronto may see continued strength today from the financial sector and paper and forest products companies, which should benefit from higher pulp prices.

In economic news, Statistics Canada reported today that foreign investors sold a net C$3.47 billion in Canadian securities in May after buying a net C$3.96 billion in April (revised from C$4.18 billion).
--- STOCKS TO WATCH ---

* Potash Corp of Saskatchewan Inc reported second-quarter earnings of US$1.81 per share, up from US$1.15 a share in the same period last year. The fertilizer company said strong volumes so far in 1997 should result in higher prices going forward.
* Methanex Corp reported late on Wednesday second- quarter earnings of US$0.34 a share, up from US$0.06 a share in the second quarter of 1996.
